whatIsIt.eli5: YOLO12's main team block. Its helpers let spots look at each other, but only inside a few big strips, which keeps it fast.
whatIsIt.simple: YOLO12's block (R-ELAN). A 1×1 Conv, then a chain of units; each unit is two attention blocks (area attention + MLP) or, in some layers, a C3k. All outputs are joined and mixed. Large models add a scaled shortcut around the whole block.
whatIsIt.engineer: cv1 (1×1, c_=c2·e) → n units [Seq(ABlock, ABlock) if a2 else C3k] chained → cat[(1+n)·c_] → cv2 (1×1); if a2 and residual (l/x): y = x + γ·cv2(…) with γ init 0.01.

whyExists.eli5: Looking at the whole picture is useful, and strips make it cheap enough to use on bigger maps.
whyExists.simple: The YOLO12 paper builds the detector around attention. Area attention splits the map into a few regions so attention is affordable at P4; R-ELAN's scaled residual keeps large attention models stable while training.
whyExists.engineer: Attention-centric design; area attention reduces cost by ~l; block-level residual with layer scaling (R-ELAN) addresses optimisation instability of large models (paper §3).

eli5: Each helper lets spots in the same strip look at each other.
Keep every helper's work, stack and summarize.
simple: cv1 (1×1 Conv) to the hidden width.
Each unit: two ABlocks (area attention, then a small MLP, each with a shortcut).
Every unit's output is kept; join all (1 + n pieces).
cv2 (1×1 Conv) to the output width.
For l/x: add the input back, scaled by γ (starts at 0.01).
engineer: Heads = c_/32; area = 4 at P4, 1 at P5 in yolo12.yaml (area 1 = global attention).
MLP ratio 2.0 by default; parse_model passes (residual=True, mlp_ratio=1.2) for l/x.
a2=False rows (neck in yolo12.yaml) use C3k units instead of attention.

example.eli5: In YOLO12n layer 6, the 40×40 picture is cut into 4 strips.
example.simple: YOLO12n layer 6: 128 channels at 40×40, area = 4, 180,864 parameters. Layer 8 (20×20, area = 1): 689,408 parameters.

typicalPositions.eli5: In the later part of the backbone and in the mixing part.
typicalPositions.simple: YOLO12 backbone at P4 and P5 (attention on) and the neck (attention off, C3k units).
typicalPositions.engineer: yolo12.yaml layers 6, 8 (a2=True) and neck fusion nodes (a2=False).

tradeoffs.eli5: Looking around costs more than looking nearby.
tradeoffs.simple: Attention cost grows with the square of the positions per area; Ultralytics notes YOLO12 can be slower on CPUs and use more memory.
tradeoffs.engineer: O((N/l)²·d·l) per head; memory heavy without FlashAttention.
